findings.title: Keystroke gate is graded in an ingest order the app never runs; keystroke onsets escape suppression live, no false trigger observed
findings.demonstration: Tests/TunkCoreTests/AuditGateOrderTests.swift (kept, passes; output quoted). The harness delivers every input before any sample with t_ns >= input.t_ns (Replay.swift:166-169; TapDetector.replayGroups Detector.swift:662-673). Live, samples enter Engine.feed(sample:) on the sensor queue ~0.3 ms after their stamp and a keystroke enters Engine.feed(input:) on main only after NSEvent global-monitor delivery lag L, which the project records as never measured (web/progress.json:8205). Detector.ingest(input:) only retracts onsets at or BEFORE the input stamp (`input.tNs >= last && input.tNs - last <= preGateNs`, Detector.swift:275-283), and an onset accepted earlier was tested against a gateUntilNs that did not yet include this key (Detector.swift:438). Engine.feed(input:) then clamps the stamp forward to the start of the newest 8.33 ms display bucket (`e.tNs = max(e.tNs, ringBucket * Engine.bucketNs)`), which the harness does not do. Measured on the three data/raw typing sessions with the shipped detector armed {2}: the detector's onset is stamped AFTER its keyDown for 93 % (desk, p50 +6.2 ms), 55 % (lap, p50 +5.9 ms) and 80 % (soft, p50 +11.5 ms) of matched strikes, so live ingest order is reversed for most keystrokes whenever L exceeds ~6 ms. Triggers stay 0 at every L on all three recordings and on a synthetic 150 ms pair at four bucket phases: each escaped strike forms a one-onset group that the following keyUp's 180 ms gate keeps from pairing. So 'fires while typing' is a demonstrated all-clear for L <= 60 ms on this corpus; what is demonstrated is that live gate coverage is weaker than the graded one and that live and replay are not the same code path for the gate.
findings.fix: Make the gate order-independent so replay equals live: in Detector.ingest(input:), also clear the live group when groupLastOnsetNs is in (input.tNs, input.tNs + gateWindowNs], and mark pending / the last onsetLog entry suppressed on the same test; in harness order such onsets were already suppressed on acceptance, so replay results do not move (check with tunk-score run --check-determinism plus the byte-identical held-out report). Then drop the forward clamp in Engine.feed(input:), which only exists because the detector cannot look forward.
